_description: Student's t return distribution with df=3 (very heavy tails) and high volatility, combined with a withdrawal stream that eats into the portfolio. df=3 sits at the edge where variance is finite but kurtosis is infinite, so extreme downside years happen significantly more often than under log-normal. Paired with a steady spending draw, this produces a visibly lower success probability than the log-normal case.
_rationale: 80/20 portfolio starting at $800,000 with 7% stockReturn / 20% stockStdDev, $50,000/yr living expenses (no income), 25-year horizon. Blended deterministic return ≈ 6.2%; deterministic balance would grow modestly. Under log-normal the 20% stock stddev already produces meaningful downside; under standardized-t with df=3 the tail kurtosis inflates large-loss frequency, driving more runs to depletion. Expected probability: noticeably below 100% — range 60–95 is wide enough to tolerate PRNG variation while still asserting the t-distribution path is active and producing non-trivial failure rates. Median final balance range is broad because heavy tails widen the run-to-run distribution.
name: Fat Tail: Extreme (df=3)
